newsitem.title: USA: Congress to pass tax bill Clinton will sign - Armey.
newsitem.headline: Congress to pass tax bill Clinton will sign - Armey.

text.p: U.S. House Majority Leader Richard Armey said Tuesday he expected Congress would pass a tax bill that President Clinton would sign.
"I think we will be able to work out an agreement that ... in the end we will pass a bill the president will sign," the Texas Republican said at a press briefing.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, who has criticized House and Senate tax legislation on behalf of the Clinton administration, is more adamant on some issues than the White House, Armey said. "I think the secretary probably has a greater level of adamancy on some provisions than the White House does," he said.
House and Senate negotiators will start meetings at the end of this week to work out differences in their two tax bills so one final bill can be passed and sent to Clinton.

Armey said he did not know what the outcome will be of a provision in the House bill to index capital gains for inflation that is not in the Senate version and is opposed by the White House. He also would not predict the outcome of a cigarette tax increase that is included in the Senate bill but not in the House version.
"I don't want a veto on anything," Armey said. "The White House will be consulted throughout the entire process," he added.
